scenario: Sep 21: Reuters says Saudi exports recovered above 4 million bpd in September and Hormuz-bound Saudi oil averaged 2.9 million bpd over the past six days, but Houthi attacks on Riyadh and Yanbu and the US-Iran stalemate keep routing risk high. Brent is $97.49 (-1.81%) and WTI $94.04 (-2.12%) on Sep 21; JKM CFD is $27.51 (+2.84%) and TTF is 79.52 EUR/MWh (+4.15%) on latest Sep 18 observations. The official $22.00 Reuters September-delivery assessment remains carried. QatarEnergy force majeure remains through November while it seeks 2-3 MTPA of US LNG through 2031. Crisis level remains 4 (High); base 15%, stress 45%, tail 40%.

categories.label: Food & Agriculture
categories.supplyChainImpact: Middle East fertilizer and energy exports remain constrained while The National's Sep 14 review reported four vessels out and 10 in over the weekend against a 14-vessel 10-day Hormuz average. Iran-Gulf talks were shelved because conditions were not right; Washington's sanctions pressure and QatarEnergy force majeure through November sustain freight and input-cost risk for Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia planting chains.

categories.label: Petrochemicals & Plastics
categories.supplyChainImpact: SABIC, QAPCO and Omani exporters depend on Gulf shipping, while Southeast Asian crackers rely on Gulf condensate and naphtha. The National reported Iran-Gulf talks were shelved and weekend Hormuz traffic remained below the 14-vessel 10-day average. QatarEnergy force majeure through November and the direct tanker war add compliance, feedstock and routing uncertainty for plastics, packaging and agrochemicals.

categories.label: Shipping & Freight
categories.supplyChainImpact: P&I war-risk constraints continue to divert or delay Gulf shipping as the direct tanker war persists and Iran-Gulf talks remain shelved. Reuters reported Sep 16 that Saudi Aramco is rerouting crude through Hormuz via Sohar ship-to-ship transfers after a Sep 11 drone strike shut its East-West pipeline, and Sep 17 that Hormuz tanker crossings remain in single digits amid a record VLCC ordering wave (217 in 2026 vs 93 in 2025). Reuters' Sep 11 report carries a route-specific Gulf of Oman-to-China VLCC assessment near Worldscale 450, roughly $11.50/bbl; the displayed AG-Asia WS105 estimate and current LNG freight remain outside the commercial evaluation because no matching route-normalised close is approved.

assets.name: Baltic Dry Index
assets.narrative: The latest reviewed BDI observation is 3,107 points from Aug 27 (Trading Economics), up 1.67%; it is carried and measures broad dry-bulk conditions, not a route-normalised Hormuz freight cost.

assets.name: VLCC AG-Asia Rate
assets.narrative: The displayed WS105 level remains an estimate from Jul 24 and is not used in the commercial evaluation because no matching route-normalised TD3C close is approved. Reuters separately reported a Gulf of Oman-to-China VLCC assessment near WS450, roughly $11.50/bbl, on Sep 11; it is carried as a different route. Reuters reported Sep 17 that industry-wide VLCC spot rates have climbed above $500,000/day (Allied Shipbroking) since the Sep 11 Saudi pipeline attack, with 217 VLCCs ordered in 2026 versus 93 in 2025. Source: Seatrade Maritime/Clarkson estimate; Reuters/Baltic Exchange route observation.

assets.name: Container Freight (SCFI)
assets.narrative: The latest reviewed SCFI observation remains 1,480 points from Jul 24. It is a weekly container benchmark and does not establish current Gulf war-risk or rerouting costs. Source: Shanghai Shipping Exchange, carried.
